# Part I: The Machine {.unnumbered}

Physical AI begins where computation ceases to be symbolic and becomes physical force. When an algorithm writes to a memory-mapped register on a pulse-width modulation timer, an H-bridge switches, current surges into motor windings, and mass accelerates under gravity and momentum. At that boundary, the forgiving conventions of software engineering—where errors can be caught by exceptions, retried in background loops, or patched post-crash—are superseded by the conservation laws of physics. Matter will not pause for an operating system scheduler, and inertia does not negotiate with neural network inference jitter.

This first part of the book constructs the structural container of the machine. It derives the physical, computational, and architectural foundations that make embodied autonomy possible, establishing why physical safety must be settled in hardware rather than promised by learned weights.

### The Three Pillars of Part I
 
Following the foundational boundary established in Chapter 1, Part I progresses across three core chapters that construct the physical apparatus of the machine:

* **Chapter 2: Body (*What the Physical World Will Not Allow*):** Measures the five non-negotiable physical limits of the mechanical plant: measurement age, stopping distance kinematics, actuator torque and slew saturation, thermal accumulation duty cycles, and electrical bus brownout margins.
* **Chapter 3: Brain (*What a Learned Component Gives You, and What It Costs*):** Treats the neural model as an untrusted, unprivileged machine component, specifying its input/output contracts, Expected Calibration Error, inference memory and bandwidth costs, and the canonical five-stage handoff sequence.
* **Chapter 4: Nervous System (*Who Is Allowed to Move the Motors*):** Reconciles the unyielding Body with the stochastic Brain, deriving multi-rate execution cadences ($1000\text{ Hz}$, $10\text{--}100\text{ Hz}$, $1\text{--}10\text{ Hz}$) from physical time constants, isolating hardware register privilege, and assembling the **5x5 Grid of Handoffs and Limits** that governs the entire text.

### What You Will Master in Part I

By the conclusion of Part I, you will possess a rigorous mental model of physical autonomy:

1. **The Principle of Proposal and Permission:** A learned model is strictly a proposer of candidate action chunks; only deterministic hardware enforcers possess the physical privilege to commit register writes.
2. **Deriving Rates from Physics:** Control frequencies are dictated by actuator time constants $\tau = L/R$, structural resonances, and photon integration windows, never chosen arbitrarily for software convenience.
3. **The 5x5 Synthesis Matrix:** Every signal path in an embodied machine maps to an intersection between five canonical handoffs (*Sensing $\to$ Perception $\to$ State $\to$ Plan $\to$ Enforce*) and five physical limits (*Latency, Bandwidth, Energy/Thermal, Determinism, Fault Domain*).
